preserved_attempts.root_cause: an analyzer-only common-interval assertion was accidentally located inside the role-local speed function

four diagnostic ranks intentionally sharing one GPU narrowly exceeded a three-second common interval; the interval was conservatively frozen at ten seconds while preserving the exact slowdown and peer-change gates
JSON serialization changed descriptor shape tuples to lists and a raw dictionary comparison rejected all otherwise identical rank catalogs
the role harness read the publication leaf directly although the coordinator intentionally returns it beneath the publication summary namespace

the role harness constructed a second LearnerRuntime with an RNG object whose single-owner guard correctly rejected rebinding; the corrected harness reuses the original runtime and swaps only its safe-boundary observer

the first integrated timing harness invoked adoption before snapshot publication at one safe boundary; adoption correctly changed the progress vector and the publisher then rejected the now-stale boundary event. The corrected observer order snapshots the boundary first and applies any pending adoption second, matching the established in-flight old-base contract.

rationale: The sixth one-node diagnostic passed, but the independent Checker blocked Phase A because the evidence path did not yet measure integrated publication/adoption/syncer timing, decode encoded authoritative numeric inputs and compound successors, or instrument all evaluation restart reads. The first correction run exposed and preserved a deterministic safe-boundary observer-order violation before its second step. The final reserved one-node validation checks the corrected established snapshot-then-adopt order before the same Checker is asked to reconsider formal admissibility. No algorithm, acceptance threshold, formal topology, or formal allowance changes.
